_doc: T-143 (UPDATE 09 section 4): more people on Map 0 (Crossroads Inn) and Kaltenbrunn, as ExtraPerson nodes (gravelight/world/extra_person.gd; ExtraPeople reads this table). Kept apart from companions.json on purpose: a MapCompanion JOINS the squad (a Player body, a brain, a pid), these stay where they are: a PatronBody (a modelled person from people.json, no new body pipeline, no collider, nothing to push) with a Talk card (PersonCard) and, mostly, one favour. Offline only, like the companions. Per person: maps (map id prefixes), name / title / bio (the Talk card), speaker (VO code, voice_cast.json) and lines (category PEOPLE_<KIND>), bodies (the first one speaks; person = a people.json id, look = the primitive fallback colours, pose), appear_round, favour {kind fetch: item_at is where the item lies once the favour is accepted; reward.kind scrip | scrip_mark | revive_point | intel_ping | cover | unbolt_door; reward.rounds = how many rounds it lasts}, trade {cost, once_per_round} (the courier's tip). poi = the minimap marker label. All positions are in the map generator's frame and are checked on the navmesh by NpcWallProbe (and test_people_extra).

miners.name: Alois Brzezina and two miners
miners.title: ALOIS BRZEZINA
miners.speaker: MIN
miners.bio: A Silesian shift boss and two of his hewers, hired men from the villages round the mine, not guards and not prisoners. When the bell rang on 20 December they stayed where they were, in an old side gallery with a dead lamp, and have been quiet since. Brzezina knows every working in the mine and has worked with Jakub's gang.

favour.ask: Our lamp is dead. A safety lamp hangs by the bunks in the barracks. Bring it, and I will chalk you a short way.
favour.have: You have the lamp. Give it to Brzezina?
favour.done: They keep the lamp lit low. Brzezina chalked a way through the old workings on your map.

medic.name: Matthias Roth, medic
medic.title: MATTHIAS ROTH
medic.speaker: MED
medic.bio: A medical orderly of the garrison's infirmary, 40, who stayed with the sick and wounded in the barracks when his unit pulled out. He wears no insignia, only a white apron over his tunic; he treated the labour gangs' injured too, on the quiet, and says so to no one.

favour.ask: My linen is gone. There is a crate of bandages from the infirmary at the far end of the bunks. Fetch it.
favour.have: You have the bandages. Hand them to Roth?
favour.done: For two rounds Roth will get to anyone who goes down within reach of the bunks.

radio.name: Marta Seidl, switchboard operator
radio.title: MARTA SEIDL
radio.speaker: RAD
radio.bio: The mine's civilian telephonist, 30, who was at her board when the line to Breslau went dead and a voice that is not human began to count on it. She still plugs the jacks in and out, listening. She relays what the Operator says, in her own words, to anyone who will hear.

favour.ask: My set lost its valve. There is a spare in the radio room upstairs, on the desk. Bring it down and I will listen for you.
favour.have: You have the valve. Fit it to Seidl's set?
favour.done: The set hums. Seidl sweeps the line once and marks where the dead are gathering.

deserter.name: Gerd Lanz, a deserter
deserter.title: GERD LANZ
deserter.speaker: DES
deserter.bio: Nineteen, walked away from a column on the carters' road and has been hiding in the hayloft since the snow. No uniform left to speak of, no insignia, no gun. He wants to see the spring, and he will fight for it if someone trusts him with a rifle.

favour.ask: Give me a rifle and I will watch the stable door. I owe somebody, and it may as well be you.
favour.have: Hand Lanz the gun in your hands? He keeps it.
favour.done: Lanz has the gun and covers the stable door for the rest of this round.

widow.name: Hanne Ebert, a carter's widow
widow.title: HANNE EBERT
widow.speaker: WID
widow.bio: Sixty, the widow of the last salt carter on this road. She took a room above the taproom the autumn he died and stayed. Her husband went out to the yard for his lamp the night the plane came down, and she has not unlatched the side door since.

favour.ask: His lamp hangs on the cart in the yard. Bring it to me, and I will draw the bolt on the side door.
favour.have: You have the carter's lamp. Give it to Ebert?
favour.done: Ebert draws the bolt: the kitchen back door opens free for two rounds.

courier.name: Lotte Hager, a courier
courier.title: LOTTE HAGER
courier.speaker: COU
courier.bio: A district courier, 25, bicycle post for the villages, stuck at the carters' gate with a snapped chain and a canvas bag of letters. She has ridden every road in the district and knows where things are left; she trades what she has seen for Scrip.

pohl.name: Obergefreiter Pohl, the Kranich's wireless operator
pohl.title: OBERGEFREITER POHL
pohl.speaker: OGP
pohl.bio: The Kranich's wireless operator, 22, Riedl's man at the set. The field units hung the crew on the racks in Fulfillment with the rest of the inventory, and Pohl did not go to sleep. He climbed down out of bay six and has stood in the aisle beside it since, keeping out of the way, keeping very still when the dead go past. He does not fight. He asks for one thing: that somebody reads his name into the record, so that it says Pohl and not a number.

favour.ask: My tag is still on the hanger, on the wrist. Take it to their console in the Account, before you do whatever you are going to do there. There is a slot. Read it in. So it says Pohl. Not rack two, bay six.
favour.have: You carry Pohl's tag. The slot is on the console's dais in the Account: read it in before the end.
favour.done: Pohl's name is in the record. Somewhere in the relay a number becomes a man again.

dee._doc: UPDATE 10 §3 Act III (T-157): Sgt. Dee Marchetti in her supply cage (the body behind the counter is fixed; she is talked to at the counter, talk_at). Her favour: the valve for her field radio from the motor pool; she calls in one supply drop at the hangar.
dee.name: Sgt. Dee Marchetti, supply
dee.title: SGT. DEE MARCHETTI
dee.speaker: DEE
dee.bio: The range's supply sergeant, 31, from Paterson, New Jersey. She locked herself in the hangar's supply cage the night the lab went quiet and has run the range from behind the wire since: the radio, the side door, the generator's fuel. She keeps a ledger of everything and lets nothing go to waste.

favour.ask: My field radio's dead without its valve. There's a spare in the motor pool, in the parts box behind the second truck. Bring it here and I'll get you something.
favour.have: You have the valve. Hand it through the wire?
favour.done: Dee calls in a supply drop: one crate at the hangar. She only gets the one.

hale._doc: UPDATE 10 §3 Act III (T-157): Mr. Hale in his glass office: a Talk card only (no favour), cold; he reacts to Peg's choice (peg_resigned / peg_delivered). Talked to at the office's east face (talk_at); his body behind the glass is fixed.
hale.name: Mr. Hale, the program
hale.title: MR. HALE
hale.speaker: HAL
hale.bio: A civilian with a Washington pass and no department anyone can name, 50s, grey suit, the only clean collar on the range. He signs for everything himself. He had a man waiting at the siding in Thalbach for the British crate and he has a man waiting for you.
hale.said: Hale does not offer you a chair. He has nothing for you, and he tells you so very politely.

reactions.said: Peg kept the engine. Hale writes something down and does not look up. 'Considerable strain, Lieutenant. It's in the file.'
Peg gave him the engine. Hale is almost warm about it, which is worse. 'Your country is in your debt.'
